mcqs.question: What problem does momentum solve compared to plain SGD?
options: It smooths noisy, zig-zagging gradient updates by using a running average of past gradients
It removes the need to shuffle training data
It eliminates the need for a loss function
It guarantees convergence to the global minimum
mcqs.explanation: Momentum accumulates a running average of past gradients so updates move more consistently in one direction, damping the oscillation plain SGD shows on narrow, curved loss surfaces. It doesn't touch the loss function, data shuffling, or provide any global-minimum guarantee.

mcqs.question: You're chasing the absolute best final test accuracy on a well-studied image classification benchmark and have time to tune carefully. What's the more common expert choice?
options: Adam with default settings, since it always gives the best final accuracy
Well-tuned SGD with momentum and a learning-rate schedule, since it often generalizes better despite slower early progress
A fixed learning rate with no optimizer-specific tuning at all
Whichever optimizer trains fastest in the first epoch
mcqs.explanation: Adam converges quickly and needs less tuning, which is great for iteration speed, but carefully tuned SGD+momentum with a schedule often reaches better final generalization on vision benchmarks — which is why many state-of-the-art vision results still use it. Picking purely on first-epoch speed ignores the generalization trade-off.

mcqs.question: Training loss dropped quickly at first, then started oscillating around a plateau without settling further, even after many more epochs. What is the most likely fix?
options: Train for many more epochs at the same fixed learning rate
Switch to a larger batch size only
Reduce or decay the learning rate so later updates can settle into the minimum instead of overshooting it
mcqs.explanation: Oscillation around a plateau is the classic sign of a learning rate too large to let the optimizer settle — decaying it lets later steps take finer moves. Simply training longer at the same rate, changing batch size, or removing regularization don't address the actual overshoot mechanism.
